description: Folder that holds instances, backups and panel data.
Docker image of Odoo; the tag is the Odoo version.
Versions offered: "auto" (every published version of the official image from odoo_min_version) or a comma-separated list such as 17.0,18.0,saas-18.2.
Oldest version offered when odoo_versions is "auto".

Download the Odoo image of every offered version, and the PostgreSQL image, in the background, so the first instance of a version does not wait for the download (each Odoo image takes 1-3 GB of disk).

How often, in hours, the panel checks Docker Hub in the background for a newer Odoo image of every version in use (and of the default version for new instances). New instances use the newest image on this server at once; existing instances keep theirs until Update Odoo and PostgreSQL images.
Docker image of each instance's database.
Password of the Odoo user "admin" in new instances.
Processor weight of production instances (Docker cpu_shares; 1024 is Docker's default). Only acts when the processor is busy: a container gets processor time in proportion to its weight.
Processor weight of staging instances (Docker cpu_shares; 1024 is Docker's default). Only acts when the processor is busy: a container gets processor time in proportion to its weight.
Processor weight of development instances (Docker cpu_shares; 1024 is Docker's default). Only acts when the processor is busy: a container gets processor time in proportion to its weight.

Out-of-memory score adjustment of production instances (-999 to 1000): when the server runs out of memory, the kernel stops processes with the highest score first. -1000 (never stopped) is not allowed.
Out-of-memory score adjustment of staging instances (-999 to 1000): when the server runs out of memory, the kernel stops processes with the highest score first. -1000 (never stopped) is not allowed.

Out-of-memory score adjustment of development instances (-999 to 1000): when the server runs out of memory, the kernel stops processes with the highest score first. -1000 (never stopped) is not allowed.
Memory reservation of the Odoo container of production instances (Docker mem_reservation, a soft limit): under memory pressure the kernel takes memory back from other containers first. 0: none.
Memory reservation of the database container of production instances (Docker mem_reservation, a soft limit): under memory pressure the kernel takes memory back from other containers first. 0: none.
Memory reservation of the Odoo container of staging instances (Docker mem_reservation, a soft limit): under memory pressure the kernel takes memory back from other containers first. 0: none.
Memory reservation of the database container of staging instances (Docker mem_reservation, a soft limit): under memory pressure the kernel takes memory back from other containers first. 0: none.
Memory reservation of the Odoo container of development instances (Docker mem_reservation, a soft limit): under memory pressure the kernel takes memory back from other containers first. 0: none.
Memory reservation of the database container of development instances (Docker mem_reservation, a soft limit): under memory pressure the kernel takes memory back from other containers first. 0: none.
Default for production instances. Odoo HTTP workers (odoo.conf workers); 0: threaded mode, Odoo's default.
Default for production instances. Odoo cron workers (odoo.conf max_cron_threads); 0: Odoo's default (2).
Default for production instances. Memory per Odoo worker before it is recycled, in MB (limit_memory_soft); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for production instances. Memory per Odoo worker before a request is stopped, in MB (limit_memory_hard); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for production instances. Processor seconds one request may use (limit_time_cpu); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for production instances. Seconds one request may take (limit_time_real, the HTTP timeout); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for production instances. Memory the Odoo container may use, in Docker units (512m, 2g); 0: no limit.
Default for production instances. Processor cores the Odoo container may use; 0: no limit.
Default for production instances. Memory the database container may use, in Docker units (512m, 2g); 0: no limit.
Default for production instances. Processor cores the database container may use; 0: no limit.
Default for production instances. Seconds one scheduled action may run (limit_time_real_cron); 0: Odoo's default (the same as limit_time_real).

Default for production instances. Connections the database accepts (PostgreSQL max_connections); Odoo's db_maxconn is then shared out between its processes. 0: PostgreSQL's and Odoo's defaults (100, 64).
Default for staging instances. Odoo HTTP workers (odoo.conf workers); 0: threaded mode, Odoo's default.
Default for staging instances. Odoo cron workers (odoo.conf max_cron_threads); 0: Odoo's default (2).
Default for staging instances. Memory per Odoo worker before it is recycled, in MB (limit_memory_soft); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for staging instances. Memory per Odoo worker before a request is stopped, in MB (limit_memory_hard); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for staging instances. Processor seconds one request may use (limit_time_cpu); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for staging instances. Seconds one request may take (limit_time_real, the HTTP timeout); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for staging instances. Memory the Odoo container may use, in Docker units (512m, 2g); 0: no limit.
Default for staging instances. Processor cores the Odoo container may use; 0: no limit.
Default for staging instances. Memory the database container may use, in Docker units (512m, 2g); 0: no limit.
Default for staging instances. Processor cores the database container may use; 0: no limit.
Default for staging instances. Seconds one scheduled action may run (limit_time_real_cron); 0: Odoo's default (the same as limit_time_real).

Default for staging instances. Connections the database accepts (PostgreSQL max_connections); Odoo's db_maxconn is then shared out between its processes. 0: PostgreSQL's and Odoo's defaults (100, 64).
Default for development instances. Odoo HTTP workers (odoo.conf workers); 0: threaded mode, Odoo's default.
Default for development instances. Odoo cron workers (odoo.conf max_cron_threads); 0: Odoo's default (2).
Default for development instances. Memory per Odoo worker before it is recycled, in MB (limit_memory_soft); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for development instances. Memory per Odoo worker before a request is stopped, in MB (limit_memory_hard); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for development instances. Processor seconds one request may use (limit_time_cpu); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for development instances. Seconds one request may take (limit_time_real, the HTTP timeout); 0: Odoo's default.
Default for development instances. Memory the Odoo container may use, in Docker units (512m, 2g); 0: no limit.
Default for development instances. Processor cores the Odoo container may use; 0: no limit.
Default for development instances. Memory the database container may use, in Docker units (512m, 2g); 0: no limit.
Default for development instances. Processor cores the database container may use; 0: no limit.
Default for development instances. Seconds one scheduled action may run (limit_time_real_cron); 0: Odoo's default (the same as limit_time_real).

Default for development instances. Connections the database accepts (PostgreSQL max_connections); Odoo's db_maxconn is then shared out between its processes. 0: PostgreSQL's and Odoo's defaults (100, 64).
The most a project owner may set for Odoo HTTP workers, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.
The most a project owner may set for cron workers, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the memory per worker before recycling, in MB, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the memory per worker, in MB, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the processor time per request, in seconds, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the HTTP timeout, in seconds, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the scheduled actions timeout, in seconds, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the Odoo container's memory (Docker units), per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the Odoo container's cores, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the database container's memory (Docker units), per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the database container's cores, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

The most a project owner may set for the database connections, per project or per branch (projects.resources). Administrators' stage defaults and an instance's own limits are not bound by it. 0: no maximum.

With Odoo workers, give the Odoo container a memory and processor limit computed from them when none is set: resources_base_memory_mb + (workers + cron workers) x memory per worker before recycling, and max(1, workers) cores. A limit set anywhere wins.
The Odoo container's memory beside its workers, in MB, in the computed limit.
Refuse a resources change that raises the memory reserved by all instances above what the server can spare for them (capacity's usable memory). Lowering is always allowed.
Share of the memory of staging and development instances counted as reserved (they pause when unused); production always counts fully.
Minutes between two measurements of an instance's database and files.
Soft storage quota of a production instance (database + files), in GB; 0: none. Alerts only: nothing is refused.
Soft storage quota of a staging instance, in GB; 0: none.
Soft storage quota of a development instance, in GB; 0: none.
Share of its storage quota from which an instance is shown and alerted as almost full.
Processes and threads one instance container may run at the same time.
Size of a container log file before it is rotated (10m).
Rotated log files kept per container.

What happens when an instance's containers or files were changed outside the panel: "warn" (report it) or "restore" (report it, then recreate Odoo and its database from the panel's own configuration). Connectors are only ever reported.
Where Enterprise add-ons come from: "folder", "git" or "none".
folder source: where the add-ons of a version are; {version} (19.0) and {major} (19) are replaced.
git source: repository holding one branch per Odoo version.
git source: branch name of a version, e.g. {version}.
Module whose presence proves the add-ons are there.

How people reach the panel and the instances: "direct" (this server answers on ports 80 and 443 itself), "proxy" (your own reverse proxy or load balancer in front) or "tunnel" (an outgoing tunnel, for servers that cannot open ports).
cloudflare-quick: connector image.
cloudflare-quick: container name prefix.
cloudflare-quick: first status port of a connector.
cloudflare-quick: status port of the panel connector.
host-ports: the server's public name or address.
host-ports: scheme of the public addresses.
What starts code updates, comma-separated: "polling", "github-app" (the GitHub App's webhook), "github-webhook" (one webhook per repository).
github-webhook: the secret entered on GitHub (20 or more random characters).
Where the panel keeps its own data: "sqlite".
How user names and passwords are checked: "local" (the panel's accounts).
Second factors offered at sign-in, comma-separated: "email", "totp" or both.
Who must use a second factor: "none", "admins" or "everyone".
How the panel sends e-mail: "smtp" or "none".
Sender of the panel's e-mails, e.g. Sudoo.sh <no-reply@example.com>.
smtp: the mail server; empty: no e-mail (and no e-mail codes).
smtp: port (587 for STARTTLS, 465 for SSL).
smtp: encryption.

Let the Odoo of a Kubernetes instance send e-mail through the panel's outgoing mail server (SMTP_HOST and SMTP_PORT): "off" (nothing leaves, as before), "production" (production instances only) or "all". Only that server's addresses on that port are opened, nothing else; applied the next time an instance is started or updated.
smtp: user name, usually the full e-mail address.
smtp: password or app password.
Folder with a layout.html that replaces the built-in frame of every e-mail.
Hours an invitation link works before it expires (it works once).
When administrators may set a new account's password instead of inviting the person by e-mail: "no_mail" (only while e-mail is not set up), "always" or "never".
Invitations one administrator may send (new or again) per hour.
Recovery codes made for an account that uses an authenticator app.
E-mail people each time their account signs in (when e-mail is set up).
People may turn the sign-in e-mail off for their own account.
How accounts sign in unless an administrator chose otherwise for one, comma-separated: "password", "email_code" (a code sent by e-mail, no password) and "github" (Continue with GitHub).
The same for client accounts (people invited to follow their projects): by default a code sent by e-mail.
Offer Send me a code on the sign-in page (when e-mail is set up), for the accounts that may use it.
Sign-in codes by e-mail one address (IP) may ask for per hour.
Offer Continue with GitHub on the sign-in page. Needs the panel's GitHub App (GitHub page) with the panel's /login/github address as a callback URL.
GitHub organisations, comma-separated, whose members may sign in with GitHub without an invitation; their account is created at the first sign-in. Empty: only people with an account or invitation.
The panel role of an account created for a member of GITHUB_SIGN_IN_ORGS. Member: no rights by itself; each project's role comes from GitHub or from its Access tab.
Accept GitHub's own two-factor authentication in place of the panel's second factor, for people whose GitHub account has it on.

For accounts linked to GitHub (except administrators), a project's role follows their permission on its repository: admin gives Admin, maintain Maintainer, write Developer, triage or read Tester, none nothing. Only with GITHUB_SIGN_IN.
How often repository permissions and GitHub team members are read again.

The project role GitHub's read permission gives, for projects made from now on: viewer (can see the project) or tester (can also open Odoo on staging and development with Connect). Projects made earlier keep tester until a project Admin changes it on the project's Access tab.
The access model of new projects: "project_roles" (Viewer, Tester, Developer, Maintainer, Admin, per stage) or "legacy" (the panel role limited by the project's grant, the same in every stage).
E-mail people when they get access to a project, when their role changes, and when it ends.
People may ask a project's admins for temporary access (a higher role in one stage).
The longest temporary access that can be asked for, in hours.
E-mail each project's admins, every ACCESS_REVIEW_DAYS, who has access to it.
Days between two access reviews of a project.
Accent colour of e-mails, as #RRGGBB.
Language of the web app for accounts that have not chosen one: "en" or "ar".

Oldest version of the Sudoo.sh Licence Agreement that counts: while no super admin has accepted it (or a later one), the next super admin to sign in must accept it before anything else. Instances keep running. It cannot be newer than the version this release bundles.
Where request counts are kept: "memory".
Requests that read, per minute, per signed-in user or address; 0: no limit.
Requests that change something, per minute, per user or address; 0: no limit.
Instances on this server at most; 0: no limit.
Instances one user (or API token) may own; 0: no limit.
Minutes a user must wait between two creations; 0: no wait.
Modules one may choose to install in a new instance's database at most (the module picker of New instance and Create instance; Odoo installs their dependencies too).
Memory kept free for the operating system and Docker, in MB (the larger of this and capacity_reserve_percent is used).
Memory kept free for the operating system and Docker, in % of the server's.
Memory one running instance is counted with while none has been measured yet, in MB.
Server memory use, in %, from which the dashboard warns that instances may slow down.
Instances running at once at most: creating or starting one more is refused; 0: never refused, only warned.

Where the gateways run: "service" (their own container, sudoo-gateway: instances keep answering while the panel restarts; the panel serves them itself while that container is not running) or "embedded" (inside the panel process, as before 3.0).
service mode: seconds the gateway service may not answer the panel before the panel serves the instances itself (at once when the service stopped normally).
Largest request body a visitor may send to an instance (uploads, imports), in MB.
Seconds a visitor may send nothing while sending a request body before the gateway gives up.
Largest single WebSocket message passed to or from an instance, in MB.
Production access rules (beta): let production instances limit who may open them, by country and by address. Off: the feature is hidden and no rule applies (rules already set are kept).
When the country database is missing: "open" lets the country part of a rule pass (a warning shows in the panel), "closed" lets nobody in by country (address rules and passes still work).
Download the DB-IP Lite country database once a month while the access rules are switched on. Off: nothing is downloaded; a table already there keeps being used.
Where the monthly country database is downloaded from ({year} and {month} are filled in); an https:// address of a DB-IP country CSV file, gzip-compressed or not.

The country database counts as out of date when it was built more than this many days ago. While access rules are on and the database is missing or out of date, the panel shows a standing alert to administrators.
How long the pass given when someone opens a production instance from the panel lets their browser through its access rules, in hours.
Show visitors their full address on the blocked page (their country is always shown).
The line on the blocked page that says whom to contact; empty: built from ADMIN_CONTACT_NAME, ADMIN_CONTACT_PHONE and ADMIN_CONTACT_EMAIL.
Seconds a visitor's connection has to send a request's headers (and is kept open while idle).
Visitors' connections open at once to one instance's gateway; more are answered 503.
Visitors' connections open at once to all gateways together; more are answered 503.

Custom domains for instances: "off", "acme" (the gateway answers on ports 80 and 443 and gets a certificate for each domain from an ACME authority such as Let's Encrypt) or "external" (something in front, such as your own Cloudflare tunnel or proxy, handles https; the panel only records the domains).
The ACME authority: "production" (Let's Encrypt), "staging" (Let's Encrypt's test authority: certificates browsers do not trust, for trying things out) or the https address of another ACME directory.
Contact e-mail given to the ACME authority; empty: ADMIN_CONTACT_EMAIL, or none.
Renew a certificate this many days before it expires.
Longest wait between two attempts after a certificate could not be issued.
Custom domains one instance may have; 0: none.
The name (or address) custom domains point to; empty: PUBLIC_HOST. A name is shown as a CNAME record, an address as an A or AAAA record.
Seconds a DNS lookup of a custom domain may take.
Before asking for a certificate, check that the domain reaches this server over http (port 80), as the ACME authority will.
Port the gateway answers custom domains on over http.
Port the gateway answers custom domains on over https.

Give each instance a name under Sudoo.sh's domain (<branch>.<stage>.<company>.<base>) when the linked account's hub offers them, served with the panel's own certificates (ports 80 and 443 must reach this server). Off: no name is asked for and none is served; names held are released with their instance.
The company label asked for with the account's first managed name; empty: Sudoo.sh makes it from the company's name. It cannot change once the account has a name.
Minutes between two comparisons of the instances with their managed names.
Port of the panel: the web service (sudoo-web) listens here.
Port of the backend (127.0.0.1 only); the web service forwards to it.
Port of the live event stream (127.0.0.1 only).
First gateway port (one per instance).
First Odoo port (one per instance, 127.0.0.1 only).
Pause an instance after this many hours without visits; 0: never.
New instances pause when idle (each instance can change it).
New instances get new code automatically.
New instances upgrade changed modules after an update.
Lifetime offered for new instances, in days; 0: keep.
Instances that may be in the production stage at the same time; 0: no limit.
New production instances get new code automatically (off: updates only when someone asks, or once switched on for the instance).
Lifetime offered for new staging instances, in days; 0: keep.
Staging instances get the daily backup too (when daily_backups is on).
polling: check GitHub for new commits this often.
Production branches one project may have; 0: no limit (MAX_PRODUCTION_INSTANCES still limits the whole server).
New projects create a development instance for every new branch pushed to their repository (each project can change it).
Development instances a project creates by itself for new branches, at most at the same time (each project can change it); 0: no limit.
Development instances of projects start with Odoo's demo data (each project can change it).
A push to a staging branch: "rebuild" (a new neutralised copy of production, then the new code) or "keep_data" (only the new code, like a development instance). Each project can change it.

A branch deleted on GitHub: its development instance is kept ("keep"), backed up and switched off ("archive") or deleted after a backup ("delete"); staging is archived at most, production only marked. Each project can change it.
A push to a project's upgrade branch (named after the next Odoo version, such as 18.0) runs its database upgrade test again (each project can change it).

A new commit on a development branch: "update" (the new code in the same database, upgrading what changed), "new_build" (a new database built from scratch) or "nothing" (the commit is only recorded). Each project and branch can change it.

Modules a new development database gets: "repository" (every module of the repository), "all" (every module Odoo has, with the repository's; no tests) or "list" (only PROJECT_MODULES). Each project and branch can change it.
The modules installed when PROJECT_MODULE_INSTALL is "list", comma-separated (each project and branch can change it).
Tests of development builds: "off", "selection" (the tests of the repository's installed modules) or "custom" (PROJECT_TEST_TAGS). Each project and branch can change it.
The --test-tags of a "custom" test suite (Odoo's syntax, such as "/sale_custom,-slow"); each project and branch can change it.
Staging builds run the project's tests too, on a throw-away copy of the staging database (each project can change it).
Tests of a build that take longer are stopped and the build fails.
Builds report their result on GitHub as commit statuses (sudoo/<stage>) when the GitHub App may write statuses (each project can change it).

When a deployment triggered by a push fails (an automatic update, a rebuild on push), e-mail the person who pushed: what failed, the error details and what to do; at most once per branch and commit (each project can change it).
Before a branch goes into production, production's newest backup should be younger than this many hours (the pre-promotion checklist shows an older one in amber); 0: not checked.
Red items of the pre-promotion checklist (a failed build, another Odoo version, a lock) stop a branch from moving into production unless someone who manages the project chooses "Promote anyway".
Pull requests get a development instance of their branch (a preview), linked from a comment on the pull request and deleted when it is closed (each project can change it).
Pull-request previews one project may have at the same time (each project can change it); 0: no limit (the server's and the plan's limits still apply).
Pull requests from forks get previews too. Off by default: a fork's code is written by people outside the repository and runs on this server (each project can change it).
The repository guard's CI checks start turned on in a project that has not chosen yet (nothing reaches GitHub until a project Admin saves them). Each project can change it.
How strict the repository guard's checks are by default: relaxed (errors that break things), standard (and the usual Odoo conventions) or strict (every rule). Each project can change it.
Approvals a pull request into a production branch needs, in the branch rules the repository guard sets on GitHub (0 to 10). Each project can change it.
Approvals a pull request into a staging branch needs, in the repository guard's branch rules (0 to 10). Each project can change it.
The repository guard's production rules require a linear history (no merge commits). Each project can change it.
The repository guard's production rules require signed commits. Each project can change it.

The repository guard's production rules ask for a review by the code owners of .github/ (a CODEOWNERS entry for the project's GitHub team, people or personal account), so the workflow that makes the required check cannot be changed without review. Turn it off for a team of one. Each project can change it.

Who may push or merge to production in the repository guard's branch rules: roles (GitHub's Admin and Maintain roles) or anyone (with write access). Each project can change it, and name teams or people instead.
Failing CI checks of the repository guard stop a promotion to production (a red item of the pre-promotion checklist); off: they are shown in amber. Each project can change it.
Builds kept in the history of each branch of a project (the oldest are removed first), with the stage changes and restores since the oldest of them.

How databases may be upgraded to a newer Odoo version, comma-separated: "enterprise" (Odoo's upgrade service, with the customer's Enterprise subscription code) and "openupgrade" (OCA OpenUpgrade, Community); empty: no upgrades.
Address of Odoo's upgrade service; Odoo's upgrade script is downloaded from <address>/upgrade when an upgrade runs. Only in .env: the subscription code is sent there.
GitHub repository of OpenUpgrade (OCA, AGPL-3.0). Its sources are downloaded at the pinned commit by the temporary container that runs the upgrade, never bundled with the panel.

The OpenUpgrade commit used to upgrade to each Odoo version, as version=commit pairs, comma-separated (the commit of the repository's branch of that version); a version without one cannot be reached with OpenUpgrade.
The openupgradelib package OpenUpgrade runs with (a pip requirement).
After a production upgrade, how long Cancel the upgrade (back to the backup taken before it) is offered and Odoo is watched, rolling back by itself when it stops answering; 0: neither.
Longest time one database upgrade (Odoo's service or OpenUpgrade) may take.
Panel sign-out after this long without activity.
Longest panel session.
Who users are told to contact.
Seconds between two measurements of the server and the instances.
Back up every instance that was used since its last daily backup, once a day; each keeps only its latest daily backup.
When the daily backups run (HH:MM, 24 hours).
Time zone of the daily backup time, for example Africa/Cairo.
How long the state before a restore is kept, and Rollback offered, after a restore (hours).
Back up an instance before an update changes its code, and put it back (code, and the database when it may have changed) when the update fails.
Largest database dump that can be uploaded with Import database (GB).
Lines a log download holds at most (the last ones).
Copy backups to S3-compatible storage off this server (Cloudflare R2, AWS S3, Backblaze B2, MinIO...), each copy with a manifest of SHA-256 checksums signed with the panel's Ed25519 key.
Address of the storage's S3 API, e.g. https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com or https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com (https; http only for localhost).
Region of the bucket ("auto" for Cloudflare R2; us-east-1, eu-central-1, ... otherwise).
The bucket the copies go to (create it first; keep it private).
Folder inside the bucket for this panel's copies (several panels can share a bucket).
How the bucket is addressed: "path" (endpoint/bucket/file: R2, MinIO, B2, S3) or "virtual" (bucket.endpoint/file).
Access key ID of a key that may read and write the bucket.
The secret of that access key (stored encrypted).
Copy the backups of staging and development instances off-site too (production instances' backups are always copied while off-site copies are on).
Which backups are copied, comma-separated: manual, daily, deletion, before-update, before-restore, before-rollback, before-repair, staging-copy.
Production: keep the newest copy of each of this many most recent days.
Production: keep the newest copy of each of this many most recent months too.
Staging and development: keep the newest copy of each of this many days.
Staging and development: keep the newest copy of each of this many months too.
Download and check the newest copy of each instance again when none was verified for this many days (signature and every checksum); 0: only when someone asks.
Seconds one request to the storage may wait for an answer.
Name of this server, the main one, on the Servers page.
Region of this server, the main one (for example Frankfurt or eu-central).
Address the agents of other servers reach this panel at (https://...); empty: the panel's own public address.
Minutes a join code for a new server stays valid; it works once.
Seconds between two reports of each server's agent (status, instances, jobs).
A server whose agent has not reported for this long is shown offline.
Seconds the panel waits for a server's agent to answer a request.
Minutes a job on another server waits for the main panel when it needs it (a GitHub token), before it fails.
Instances the panel keeps of what one server's agent reports; beyond that, the rest of that server's report is not taken.
Largest description of one instance or job a server's agent may report, in KB; a larger one is not kept.
Log entries the panel takes from one server's agent per day; beyond that they are left out until the next day, which the log says once.
Largest backup an instance may have to be moved to another server, in GB.
Size of each piece of a backup copied between servers.
Moves between servers that may run at the same time.
Seconds a moved instance has to answer on its new server before the move is rolled back.
Tell people when something needs attention (a failed job, an instance down, a full disk), by e-mail and webhooks; off: no alert is sent or listed.
Send alert e-mails to every super admin with an address.
More addresses that receive alert e-mails, comma-separated (an on-call mailbox, say).
Alert when a job fails (with its plain hint and a link).
Alert when an update failed and was rolled back, or its rollback failed too.
Alert when a backup fails (manual, daily or before a change).
Alert when an instance that should run does not answer for alert_instance_down_minutes.
Minutes an instance must stay down before the alert.
Alert when the free disk falls below alert_disk_free_percent.
Alert when an instance's database and files reach storage_warning_percent of its storage quota, and again (every day for production) when they are over it.
Free disk, in % of the disk holding ODOO_ROOT, below which the alert is sent.
Alert when server memory stays above capacity_warning_percent for alert_memory_minutes.
Minutes memory must stay above the warning before the alert.
Alert when an instance was changed outside the panel (drift).
Alert when a backup could not be copied off-site, or a copy failed its check.
Alert when a production instance has had no successful off-site copy for alert_offsite_missing_hours (while off-site copies are on).
Hours without a successful off-site copy of a production instance before the alert.
Alert when the panel or a running instance has no public link for alert_public_link_minutes.
Minutes without a public link before the alert.
Alert when a custom domain's certificate cannot be issued or renewed, or expires within alert_certificate_days.
Days before a certificate expires from which it is shown and alerted as expiring.
Send a notice when a problem that was alerted is over (back online, disk freed).
The same alert is sent at most once in this many minutes; 0: every time.
E-mail one summary a day instead of each alert as it happens (webhooks and the bell still get each alert at once).
When the daily summary is sent (HH:MM, TIMEZONE).
Seconds a webhook may take to answer before the delivery counts as failed.
Webhook 1: address alerts are posted to (https).
Webhook 1: key of the X-Sudoo-Signature HMAC-SHA256.
Webhook 1: "json" (signed JSON), "slack", "discord" or "teams" (incoming webhooks).
Webhook 2: address alerts are posted to (https).
Webhook 2: key of the X-Sudoo-Signature HMAC-SHA256.
Webhook 2: "json", "slack", "discord" or "teams".
Webhook 3: address alerts are posted to (https).
Webhook 3: key of the X-Sudoo-Signature HMAC-SHA256.
Webhook 3: "json", "slack", "discord" or "teams".
People whose role allows it can open a terminal in an instance's containers from the panel (the Shell tab); off: nobody can, and open shells close.

Who may open a shell in an instance's Odoo container: "admins" (super admins and administrators), "maintainers" (and maintainers) or "developers" (and developers). Viewers never can; psql in the database container stays with super admins and administrators.
Shells in production instances: "off" (nobody), "super_admins" (super admins only) or "allowed" (whoever may open shells in other instances). Each one is confirmed when it is opened.
Super admins may open the Odoo container's shell as root (the container's capabilities stay dropped); off: every shell runs as the container's own user.
A shell nobody types in for this long closes.
Longest a shell stays open; it then closes (a new one can be opened).
Shells one person may have open at the same time.
Shells open in one instance at the same time.
Seconds the one-time ticket that connects a new shell stays valid.
Record what is typed and shown in shells: "off", "production" (shells in production instances and root shells) or "all". Recordings are encrypted; only super admins can play them.
Days recordings, and the list of past shells, are kept.
Largest recording of one shell, in MB; beyond it only what is typed is recorded, and the shell closes when that alone reaches the size again.
Space all shell recordings may take together, in MB; the oldest go first.
People whose role allows it can record what an instance's Odoo workers spend their time on (the Tools tab); off: nobody can.
Who may record a profile: "admins" (super admins and administrators), "maintainers" (and maintainers) or "developers" (and developers). Viewers never can.
Profiles of production instances may be recorded (each one is confirmed when it starts); off: only staging and development instances.
Longest recording, in minutes; people choose from 1 minute up to this.
Recordings kept per instance; the oldest is deleted when a new one is made.
Samples per second taken of each Odoo process while recording.

Container image with py-spy that records profiles (its entry point is not used: the panel runs `sh` and `py-spy` in it). Empty: the panel builds sudoo-profiler from python:3.12-slim and a pinned, hash-checked py-spy release the first time it is needed.
Most entries one export of the audit log (CSV or XLSX) contains; an export covers a year at most.

Clients confirm every major action in the portal (opening or closing, locks, emergency access, approvals, the people they let in) with a one-time link or a 6-digit code sent to their e-mail address; the action waits until then. Needs e-mail to be set up.
Minutes a client's confirmation link or code works.
The default maintenance window (HH:MM-HH:MM in TIMEZONE; it may cross midnight): planned maintenance nobody chose a time for runs at the start of the first one that fits.
The days the default maintenance window opens (comma-separated: mon,tue,wed,thu,fri,sat,sun).
When the "Tonight" and "This weekend" choices start (HH:MM in TIMEZONE).
The day the "This weekend" choice falls on.
Hours after planned maintenance arrives during which someone may choose its time before the default window applies.
The default window also applies this many hours before the deadline, if nobody chose earlier.
The soonest a chosen maintenance window may start, in minutes from now.
Reminders before maintenance starts, in hours (comma-separated); empty: no reminders.
Clients of the projects a maintenance works on get its e-mails too (planned, reminders, result).
Clients may choose the time of maintenance that works on their projects, in the client portal (confirmed by e-mail when CLIENT_CONFIRMATIONS is on).
Back up production and staging instances before maintenance updates their images.
How long a planned panel update waits for the new version to be installed (sudoo-install update) before it counts as failed, in hours.

direct and proxy: a second name of the panel for clients (portal.example.com), pointed at this server (or your proxy). There, the web app shows the client portal and only clients sign in; direct serves it on port 443 with a certificate from the ACME authority. Empty: clients use the panel's own address.
Your company's name, shown to clients at the top of the client portal and on its sign-in page; empty: the portal shows no company name.

New clients' projects start with emergency access allowed: a super admin may open a project the client closed, for a short time, by typing a reason (the client is told at once). Each client can turn it off for its projects in the portal.
How long emergency access to a closed project lasts, in minutes.
The durations offered to clients for "Open for a time", in hours (comma-separated); they may also type their own, up to client_open_max_hours.
The longest a client can open a project or branch for at once, in hours.
The duration an access request asks for unless the person changes it, in hours.
The longest duration an access request may ask for, in hours.
Hours after which an access request the client did not answer lapses (the person asks again).
Days the e-mails caught from staging and development instances are kept.
E-mails kept per instance in the mail catcher; the oldest go first.
Space the caught e-mails of one instance may take, in MB; the oldest go first.
Largest e-mail the mail catcher accepts, in MB; a larger one is refused.
Administrators may release a caught e-mail: send a copy of it, from the panel's own address, to an address they type (audit-logged); off: nobody can.
Where the documentation links of the help panel go (https).
Where Contact support goes when the panel is not linked to a Sudoo.sh account: an https:// address or a mailto: address; empty: an e-mail to ADMIN_CONTACT_EMAIL.
The help desk Contact support opens when the panel is linked to a Sudoo.sh account (https).
Where the panel sends people to compare the Sudoo.sh plans (Settings, Plan, and every message about a plan's limit) (https).
The account site where the plan of the linked account is managed and, after a downgrade, the production branches to keep are chosen (https).
Use the Sudoo.sh marketplace: register with the hub, send a signed heartbeat every 15 minutes, install plugins. Off: the panel never contacts the hub; installed free plugins keep working.
Address of the Sudoo.sh hub (https; http only for localhost while testing).
The hub's root public keys (Ed25519, base64url, comma-separated); empty: the keys this release ships for hub.sudoo.sh, or the hub's keys as first seen for another hub.
